h1: The 8 Best Cordless Electric Kettles of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best cordless electric kettles, compared on wattage, capacity, and body material so you can match one to your kitchen.
summary: The Cuisinart is our top all-rounder with 1500W and a 1.7L capacity. The Amazon Basics stainless kettle is the best value in steel, and the COMFEE' adds a full 1.7L steel body. Chefman is the choice for a bigger 1.8L glass body, and the Cosori suits buyers who want plastic and low cost.
intro: People shop for cordless kettles by looks and then discover the real differences are wattage and body material. A 1500W kettle and a 1100W kettle with the same capacity do not boil in the same time, and a glass body behaves very differently on a countertop than steel does.

We reviewed eight kettles on paper, comparing wattage, capacity, and construction from the listed specs. The ranking favors the best balance of power, size, and material, and it flags where a spec sheet leaves questions.

products.name: Cuisinart Electric Kettle
products.verdict: The strongest all-round balance of power and capacity here.
products.description:
The Cuisinart pairs a 1500W heating element with a 1.7L capacity, which is the combination most households actually need for tea, instant noodles, and pour-over coffee. It sits in the $100 to $200 price bracket.

It ranks first because it matches the top wattage in the guide without giving up capacity, while the Amazon Basics options are cheaper but offer less capacity or a different material. You pay more for that confidence.

Buy it if you boil water daily and want one kettle to cover most uses. The caveat is cost, since several picks below deliver the same 1500W and 1.7L for much less.
products.idealFor: Daily tea and coffee drinkers who want one dependable kettle.
products.skipIf: You want the same specs for under $50.

products.name: Amazon Basics Electric Stainless Steel Kettle for Tea and Coffee
products.verdict: Stainless body and 1500W at a budget price.
products.description:
This kettle has a stainless steel body, 1500W of power, and a 1L capacity, in the $25 to $50 range. It is the compact member of the group.

It lands second because the 1500W matches the Cuisinart, but the 1L capacity is smaller than the 1.7L kettles above and below it. You are trading volume for price and steel.

Best for one or two people who make a mug or two at a time. The caveat is that a full pot of tea for a group needs multiple boils.
products.idealFor: Singles and couples who want steel on a budget.
products.skipIf: You regularly boil water for more than two people.

products.name: COMFEE' Stainless Steel Electric Kettle
products.verdict: Full-size steel body with 1500W for under $50.
products.description:
The COMFEE' offers a stainless steel body, 1500W, and a 1.7L capacity, all in the $25 to $50 range. That is the same output and size as the Cuisinart in a cheaper bracket.

It ranks below the Amazon Basics steel pick on price tier equality, but above it for capacity, since 1.7L serves a household instead of one person. It trails the Cuisinart only on brand and price.

Buy it for a family or shared kitchen that wants steel and volume. The caveat is that the spec sheet lists only the basics.
products.idealFor: Families who want full capacity and steel for less.
products.skipIf: You want a smaller, lighter kettle.

products.name: Amazon Basics Electric Kettle with Glass Carafe for Tea and Coffee
products.description:
This glass carafe kettle offers 1500W and 1.7L, and it sits in the under $25 tier. Glass lets you see the water level at a glance.

It ranks fourth because it matches the COMFEE' on power and size but swaps steel for glass, which some buyers prefer and others avoid because glass is more fragile. It beats the plastic Cosori on material.

Best for budget buyers who like seeing the water. The caveat is that glass needs more careful handling than steel.
products.idealFor: Budget shoppers who want glass and full capacity.
products.skipIf: You are rough on kitchenware or have kids around.

products.name: Chefman Electric Kettle
products.verdict: The biggest capacity in the guide at 1.8L.
products.description:
Chefman gives you a glass body, 1500W, and 1.8L, the largest capacity listed in this ranking, in the under $25 tier.

It ranks below the Amazon Basics glass kettle only by narrow margin: 0.1L more capacity is a small gain, and the specs are otherwise the same. The extra volume matters for groups.

Buy it if you serve several people and want glass. The caveat is a larger body on a small counter.
products.idealFor: Households that boil for several people at once.

products.name: Cosori Electric Kettle
products.verdict: A plastic 1.7L kettle with no wattage listed.
products.description:
The Cosori is a plastic body 1.7L kettle in the $25 to $50 range. The spec sheet we have lists no wattage.

It ranks sixth because missing wattage makes it hard to compare boil speed with the 1500W picks. Plastic is lightweight but is the least premium material here.

Buy it if low weight matters and you accept the unknown on power. The caveat is exactly that gap.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a light kettle at a modest price.

products.name: OVENTE 1.7L Electric Kettle with 1100W Fast Boiling Water
products.description:
OVENTE has a stainless steel body, 1.7L, and 1100W, in the under $25 tier.

It ranks seventh because 1100W is 400W below the top picks, so expect slower heating for the same volume. It does win on price for a steel kettle.

Buy it if you want steel at the lowest cost and do not mind waiting. The caveat is lower power.
products.idealFor: Cost-focused buyers who want steel and size.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 1.7 Liter Electric Tea Kettle
products.verdict: A steel 1.7L kettle with no wattage listed.
products.description:
Hamilton Beach offers a stainless steel body and 1.7L capacity in the $25 to $50 tier. Wattage is not listed in the specs we have.

It ranks last because it matches the COMFEE' on material and size but gives no power figure, making it harder to justify over a 1500W-confirmed rival.

Buy it if you prefer the brand and verify wattage on the listing. The caveat is that missing figure.

whatMatters.detail: Wattage is the heating power, and higher means faster boiling. A 1500W kettle will outpace an 1100W one with the same capacity. Look for the wattage number in the title or bullets, not just a phrase like 'fast boil'.
Capacity in liters sets how much water you boil per cycle. A 1L kettle suits a mug or two, while 1.7L suits a household. Check the listed liters and compare to how many cups you pour at once.

Stainless steel is durable, glass shows water level but can break, and plastic is light but less premium. The material affects how the kettle ages and feels. The listing usually names the material in the title or bullets.
Larger capacity means a bigger base, which matters on a small counter. A 1.8L kettle takes more room than a 1L one. Check the listed dimensions against your available space.
A listing that omits wattage leaves you guessing at performance. Missing numbers make comparison harder. Prefer products that state wattage and capacity clearly.

faq.q: Will a cordless kettle work with any outlet?
faq.a: A 1500W kettle needs a standard household outlet. Avoid sharing the circuit with other high-draw appliances to prevent tripping a breaker.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with kettles?
faq.a: Ignoring wattage. Two kettles with the same capacity can boil at very different speeds.

faq.q: Is the Cuisinart worth it over the COMFEE'?
faq.a: On paper they match at 1500W and 1.7L. The Cuisinart costs more, so it only pays off if you prefer its brand.

faq.q: How do I set up a new kettle?
faq.a: Rinse it, boil one full batch of water, and discard it before first use. This clears manufacturing residue.

faq.q: How do I descale a kettle?
faq.a: Boil a mix of water and white vinegar, let it sit, then rinse thoroughly. Do this regularly in hard water areas.

faq.q: Can I use a kettle without a base?
faq.a: Cordless kettles lift off the base for pouring, but they heat only while seated on it. Never heat without water inside.

finalTake: The Cuisinart is the best all-around kettle on paper, thanks to 1500W and 1.7L. For most people the COMFEE' delivers the same output in steel for far less. Choose the Chefman for the biggest volume, and avoid kettles that omit wattage unless you can confirm it on the listing.
